extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent drafters/agents/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and best practices for improving the clarity of the prosecution record during patent examination, including examiner documentation habits and related drafting practices applicants can use to anticipate examiner interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced documentation of claim interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot focus: enhanced documentation of claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should document claim interpretation explicitly when terms could be construed multiple ways. This is a core Pilot emphasis to ensure the record shows how terms were interpreted during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: More detailed interview summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot focus: more detailed interview summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should provide detailed interview summaries capturing all substantive discussions. The Pilot encourages summaries that record the full substance of interviews rather than brief or vague notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: More precise reasons for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot focus: more precise reasons for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify reasons for allowance with precision, particularly when prior art rejections were overcome. Reasons should make clear how claims meet statutory requirements and why rejections no longer apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify specific limitations distinguishing claims over prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practice to identify the specific claim limitations that distinguish the claims from prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When overcoming prior art, the record should call out the particular limitations that distinguish the claims; do not rely on generalized statements. This supports transparency and reduces future ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague cross-references (e.g., 'see relevant section')
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practice to avoid using 'see relevant section' without citing specific text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should cite specific text or sections rather than using vague cross-references so that the reasoning is clear and reproducible by readers of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate and clear patentability determinations for every pending claim throughout prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality metric: deliver appropriate and clear patentability determinations for every pending claim throughout prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO aims for an impeccable work product where each pending claim has a properly documented and clearly explained patentability determination at each stage of prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend analysis on statutory compliance and clarity assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality metric: perform trend analysis on statutory compliance and clarity assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use aggregated clarity and compliance data to identify systemic issues and areas for targeted improvement across Technology Centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of underlying causes to reduce rework
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality metric: identify underlying causes of clarity or correctness issues to reduce rework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QA should seek root causes (e.g., training gaps, guidance ambiguities) so that systemic fixes can be implemented rather than only addressing individual instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality metric: promote efficiency in the prosecution process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear records and standardized practices are intended to reduce unnecessary rework and improve overall examination efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Correctness Data Capture (CCDC) Program
rubrics_metrics.description: An improved data capture system enabling consistent documentation and access to quality review data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CCDC allows OPQA and Technology Center supervisors to consistently document and access quality review data in one place, supporting uniform assessments across reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master Review Form (MRF) — correctness and clarity inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: MRF captures traditional inquiries on correctness and new inquiries on the clarity of each determination made in the Office action under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MRF is the tool used to record both statutory correctness assessments and explicit clarity judgments about each determination, enabling standardized review and data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review work products for statutory compliance, clarity, and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA assessment criterion: review work products for statutory compliance, clarity, and best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPQA reviewers evaluate examiner work products not just for legal correctness but for clarity and adherence to identified best practices to ensure a high-quality public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and standardize quality metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA responsibility: define and standardize quality metrics for assessing patent work product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized metrics allow consistent measurement across examiners and Technology Centers and support objective trend analysis and improvement efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide feedback to Technology Centers
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA role: provide feedback to Technology Centers based on QA findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback derived from clarity and correctness reviews should inform training, guidance updates, and local supervisory actions to improve overall quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafter practice — submit applications with clear claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Implication for drafters: submit applications with clear claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding examiner practices helps drafters present claims that reduce ambiguity; clear claim scope makes examiner interpretations less likely to vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafter practice — use precise language anticipating examiner interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Implication for drafters: use precise language anticipating examiner interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose wording that minimizes potential multiple constructions and anticipate how examiners may read claim terms to reduce need for later clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafter practice — provide claim charts in responses showing how amendments overcome rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Implication for drafters: include claim charts in responses that show how amendments overcome rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing clear mappings between amended claim language and prior art or rejection grounds helps the record show why rejections are overcome and supports precise allowance reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafter practice — submit precise interview summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Implication for drafters: submit precise interview summaries (when applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicants prepare or submit interview summaries, making them precise and substantive can complement examiner summaries and improve the clarity of the prosecution record.
